source.title: Feature survival under weight pruning: Sparse autoencoder diagnostics for compressed language models
source.authors: Hector Borobia; Elies Seguí-Mas; Guillermina Tormo Carbó

record.file_problem: The text is a complete paper. Its title in the text differs from the supplied title; no missing or garbled sections are apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE features as interpretability probes but does not test whether a model's own neurons have one or two main jobs, or whether neuron-based explanations explain behavior.
record.gate_note: The reported pruning results concern SAE features, not individual neuron poles or explanations tested on held-out activations. The paper does report causal ablations of SAE features; those results are recorded as related findings, not as tests of the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on residual-stream activations of pruned and dense 1–2B models and measures feature survival and ablation effects. It never audits a model's own neurons, scores explanations, builds neuron-based attribution graphs, or examines InceptionV1. SAE features are used as probes, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct but incomplete. The authors also conclude that Wanda preserves SAE feature structure up to 3.7× better than magnitude pruning. They add that official SAEs stay usable on Wanda-pruned models up to 50% sparsity, and that firing rate predicts survival (AUC > 0.79).
record.recipe_differences: Studies SAE feature geometry and causal ablations under weight pruning; it does not use the neuron-pole audit or explanation-testing procedure in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with pruning method, sparsity, and model; Wanda generally preserves feature structure better than magnitude pruning.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma 3 1B, Gemma 2 2B and Llama 3.2 1B, SAE features with high vs low dense–pruned decoder cosine match had nearly identical single-feature ablation KL (≤1.2% difference).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geometric survival of SAE features under weight pruning does not predict their causal effect on outputs.

fits_no_version.finding: Rare SAE features survive pruning far better than frequent ones (Spearman ρ = −1.0 in 11 of 17 conditions; Table 3), and seed-to-seed SAE feature MNN match is only 1.1–3.9%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under unstructured pruning, low-firing-rate SAE features are preserved more than high-firing-rate ones; SAE dictionaries are poorly reproducible across seeds.

record.problems: All models are in the 1–2B parameter range; the authors note low absolute seed-to-seed MNN rates (2–4%) and two failed deep-layer runs due to float16 overflow. Table 4 reports no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Pruning survival, firing-rate quintiles, SAE transferability, and perplexity results are not recorded as rows because they concern SAE feature geometry or model quality rather than neuron-pole interpretability or tested explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The record's T4/uses_without_test classification is right. Low seed reproducibility of SAE features (2–4% MNN) bears on SAE dictionaries, not on model neurons, so it is not linked to V6/V7.
